# Synapse 2.0.9

A fix release: nothing phones home, templates ship with every install, local models read the whole prompt, and a support widget can search its own knowledge.

## Fixed

- **Nothing phones home when Synapse starts.** Each backend start sent a usage ping to the tracking service of cocoindex, the code-search library Synapse ships. Every install now turns that off before the library loads, along with the same switches for Chroma, the Hugging Face Hub and Next.js (and `DO_NOT_TRACK`). A switch you set yourself is kept.
- **Templates ship with every install.** Workflows → Templates said "No example packs available." on pip, installer and npm installs and in the Docker images, because the example packs were left out of the package. They ship now, so Home's **Browse templates** opens all five packs.
- **Local models read the whole prompt.** Synapse sent Ollama no context size, so Ollama used its default (4,096 tokens on a small GPU) and silently cut anything longer, such as Synapse AI's planning prompt. A longer call now asks Ollama for a context that holds it, up to what the model can read; a call longer than that is refused with a sentence instead of being cut. Calls through Ollama's OpenAI-compatible `/v1` address still use `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH`.
- **A support widget can search its knowledge.** Asked for a widget whose "visitors may only search the help pages", Synapse AI's card gave visitors nothing, so the agent couldn't read its own help pages on the site, and nothing said so. Naming a knowledge base for visitors now lets them search it; a base not open to visitors is refused with where to open it; and the card says when an agent's knowledge is out of visitors' reach (also for a channel whose senders are visitors).
- **The Docker image publishes again.** 2.0.8's `synapseorchai/synapse-ai` image never published: building its web app for arm64 took longer than the release job allows. The web app is now built once, on the build machine's own platform, for every architecture, so `synapseorchai/synapse-ai:2.0.9` (and `:latest`) covers both amd64 and arm64.

## Install

**macOS and Linux**

```bash
curl -LsSf https://synapseorch.com/install.sh | bash
```

**Windows (PowerShell)**

```powershell
irm https://synapseorch.com/install.ps1 | iex
```

<details>
<summary>npm, pip or Docker</summary>

```bash
npm install -g synapse-orch-ai && synapse
pip install synapse-orch-ai && synapse         # Python 3.11–3.14 and Node.js 20.9+
```

For Docker, see [Docker](https://docs.synapseorch.com/getting-started/docker): the image is `synapseorchai/synapse-ai:2.0.9`, also `:latest`.
</details>

## Upgrading

- **From 2.0.x:** run `synapse upgrade`. Your data stays where it is, and the database is backed up first.
- **From 1.x:** run `synapse upgrade` on your 1.x install. It moves you to 2.0 the same way 2.0.0 did; read the [2.0.0 notes](https://github.com/synapseorch-ai/synapse-ai/releases/tag/v2.0.0) for what changes.

**Full changelog:** [v2.0.8...v2.0.9](https://github.com/synapseorch-ai/synapse-ai/compare/v2.0.8...v2.0.9) · [Documentation](https://docs.synapseorch.com)
